definitions.explanation: A past court decision, especially of a higher court, that serves as an example or authority for deciding later cases with similar facts. Collectively, the body of such decisions.

examples.japanese: {過去|かこ}の{判例|はんれい}を{調|しら}べる。
この{事件|じけん}には{参考|さんこう}になる{判例|はんれい}がない。
examples.english: There is no precedent that serves as a reference for this case.

examples.japanese: {最高裁|さいこうさい}の{判例|はんれい}は、その{後|ご}の{下級審|かきゅうしん}の{判断|はんだん}に{大|おお}きな{影響|えいきょう}を{与|あた}える。
examples.english: Supreme Court precedents have a great influence on the decisions of lower courts thereafter.

notes:
Composed of {判|はん} (judgment) + {例|れい} (example). Refers to prior court decisions used as a guide for later cases; Supreme Court ({最高裁|さいこうさい}) precedents carry particular weight.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {判例|はんれい}に{従|したが}う: to follow precedent
- {判例|はんれい}を{変更|へんこう}する: to overturn / change a precedent
- {判例|はんれい}{集|しゅう}: a collection of precedents; a casebook

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {前例|ぜんれい}: a precedent — the everyday word for any prior example, not limited to court decisions
- {判決|はんけつ}: a (court) judgment — a single ruling; {判例|はんれい} is a judgment treated as an authority for later cases
